newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Winterthur says no one has more than 5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Winterthur says no one has more than 5 pct.

text.p: Winterthur Insurance Co said its share register contains no shareholders with more than five percent of the company's shares.

The company also said in a statement that it was aware of BZ Group's shareholding and has already commented on it and that aside from BZ other institutional investors such as Swiss Reinsurance hold shares.
But it said none hold more than five percent, the limit set in its Articles of Association.

"Aside from BZ Group, other institutional investors such as Swiss Re hold Winterthur shares. However, our share register contains no shareholders with more than five percent of the shares, which is the limit laid down in the Articles of Association. Winterthur will continue to adhere to this policy," the company said in brief statement.
However, Swiss Re said in a statement circulated shortly after Winterthur's that "it owns about five percent of Winterthur shares oustanding".
The statements follow comments from Swiss financier Martin Ebner, who runs the BZ Group of investment funds.
Ebner said earlier that a letter he said came from Winterthur Insurance showed that Swiss Reinsurance held at least five percent of Winterthur.
Stamped as received by the BK Group on July 4, the document appeared to be a response to a request for registration of Winterthur shares recently bought by BK Vision, one of Ebner's funds.
Ebner also said his BZ Group of investment funds had raised its stake in Winterthur to 18.3 percent as of June 30 from 14.5 percent in mid-May.
The stake as of June 30 was held 11.3 percent by investment fund BK Vision and 7.0 percent by another fund, Stillhalter Vision.
Ebner told reporters that around another five percent of Winterthur registered shares was held by customers advised by the BZ Bank, the bank arm of the BZ Group.
But he declined to say whether the group had been buying this week, when Winterthur shares jumped over 7.5 percent from Monday through Thursday's close at 1,438 Swiss francs.
"All I will say is that our participation in Winterthur is not lower today than it was on June 30," he told reporters late on Thursday at a briefing on his group's six-month results.
Ebner also declined to say whether the group planned to raise its holding in Winterthur. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
